products.title: RUBY GREEN FULL SLEEVE
products.body_html:
RUBY GREEN FULL SLEEVE

RUBY GREEN FULL SLEEVE , Elevate your everyday essentials with our versatile range of T-shirts — thoughtfully designed for both full sleeve and half sleeve preferences. Whether you're dressing for the season, your lifestyle, or your personal style, these tees blend comfort, durability, and clean design into one timeless staple.

Fit & Style

Our T-shirts come in a regular fit that flatters all body types. Designed with care, they feature reinforced seams, a classic crew neck, and a silhouette that strikes the right balance between structure and flow. Whether you’re pairing it with jeans, joggers, or layering under a jacket, this T-shirt holds its shape and enhances your outfit.

Choose from solid colors, subtle prints, or minimal graphics — each curated to match your everyday wardrobe. The full sleeve tees offer a sleek, modern look that works well for casual Fridays, evenings out, or just a laid-back day. The half sleeve variants bring timeless charm, making them your go-to option for effortless dressing in warmer weather.

How to Measure T-shirt Length and Chest:

Chest:

Measure around the fullest part of your chest, under the arms and across the shoulder blades. Keep the tape flat and snug.

Length:

Measure from the top of the shoulder (near the collar) straight down to the bottom hem of the t-shirt.

MEASURING

1. Waist
Measure around the narrowest part of your waist, typically just above the belly button. Make sure the tape is snug but not tight. This is your true waist size.

2. Rise
The rise is the distance from the top of the waistband to the crotch seam. To measure, lay the jeans flat and measure from the top of the front waistband down to the crotch seam.

3.Length (OUTSEAM)

Lay the jeans flat and measure from the top of the waistband down the outside edge of the leg to the hem. This is your outseam length, which determines the overall length of the jeans.

4. Thigh
Measure across the thigh area, starting about 1–2 inches below the crotch. Multiply that number by two to get the full thigh measurement. This determines how fitted the jeans will feel on your upper legs.

5. Leg Opening
Lay one leg flat and measure across the bottom hem. Double this number to get the total leg opening. This measurement affects how the jeans fall over your shoes — from tapered to wide-leg styles.
